title: Universal Domain Entities Conflating Distinct Bounded Contexts
pattern: Different bounded contexts are forced to use one universal or monolithic domain entity because they refer to the same physical subject or use similar terminology, despite owning different meanings, rules, and data.
why_bad: A shared physical subject is mistaken for a shared domain concept (a "false cognate"). Changes cross semantic boundaries, teams step on each other's code, irrelevant optional fields proliferate, and each context must accommodate another's rules and representation.
detection: Identify structs/classes with domain-specific field clusters that are only ever accessed together by distinct, non-overlapping application services, or large records combining clearly different business vocabularies (e.g. shipping logistics vs. retail billing). Establish actual differences in model meaning or ownership rather than treating team boundaries, size, or field clusters alone as proof; distinct contexts can exist under one team.
source: *Domain-Driven Design* (Evans), Chapter 14: "duplicate concepts and false cognates", p. 410; *Domain-Driven Design* by Eric Evans (Chapter 14, p. 96).
